atypical_presentation_modifiers.source_note: SAEM/CDEM M4 geriatrics curriculum, 'Atypical presentations of critical illness in older adults'. These establish DIRECTION of effect, not magnitude.
atypical_presentation_modifiers.implementation_decision: Implemented as ESCALATE-ONLY QUALIFIERS that REMOVE REASSURANCE, never as numeric additions to the score. Blueprint 9.5 table B: 'The literature establishes the direction of these effects, not a magnitude. Implementing them as removals of reassurance is faithful to what is actually known. Assigning them point values would be inventing precision.'

modifiers.name: Absent fever does not reassure
modifiers.text: Fever and leucocytosis are often absent in acute infection because of immunosenescence. A normal temperature NEVER reassures in the geriatric envelope, at any freshness.

modifiers.name: Blunted tachycardia on rate-control medication
modifiers.text: Beta-blockers and calcium-channel blockers mask the compensatory tachycardia that would otherwise signal deterioration. Unknown is treated as possible, per Blueprint 8.1: 'Unknown -> the geriatric envelope assumes tachycardia may be masked.'

modifiers.name: Relative hypotension against baseline
modifiers.condition: baseline_bp present AND systolic_bp < baseline_systolic * (1 - relative_drop_fraction)
modifiers.text: Baseline hypertension means an apparently acceptable BP can represent acute decompensation. A BP of 104/60 is unremarkable in isolation and alarming against a usual 150/90.
modifiers.note: The DIRECTION is from [S6]. The 20% threshold is ASM - our chosen operating point, exposed as configurable.

modifiers.name: Delirium / new confusion as a presenting red flag
modifiers.condition: consciousness_acvpu == 'C' OR new_confusion reported against a documented oriented baseline
modifiers.text: Sepsis from a urinary source often presents as altered mental status in older adults. New confusion is a presenting sign, not a soft finding.

modifiers.name: New functional loss
modifiers.condition: ambulatory is false AND record indicates previously ambulatory, OR complaint indicates 'off legs' / new inability to walk
modifiers.text: Older adults present with function loss rather than symptoms. A new inability to walk is a major event regardless of vitals.

modifiers.name: Absent peritoneal signs do not exclude
modifiers.condition: abdominal complaint pathway active AND examination unremarkable
modifiers.text: Peritoneal signs are often absent in the geriatric acute abdomen.

modifiers.name: STEMI may present without chest pain
modifiers.condition: cardiac risk features present without chest pain
modifiers.text: A STEMI may present with no chest pain at all, particularly in women and older adults.

modifiers.name: Frailty modifier
modifiers.condition: frailty indicator present from a MATCHED record
modifiers.text: Two 78-year-olds with identical vitals and different frailty have materially different trajectories. Coarse frailty indicator, escalate-only, sourced from the record where identity is confirmed. Blueprint section 5 item 15 (SHOULD build).

sepsis_screening.text: qSOFA is not recommended as a single screening tool compared with SIRS, NEWS or MEWS (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence). Antimicrobials within 1 h for possible septic shock, within 3 h for possible sepsis without shock.

assumptions.text: The 20% relative-drop fraction for GER-MOD-RELHYPO is our chosen operating point. [S6] establishes that baseline-relative interpretation matters; it does not publish a percentage.
